Hi Ben and Laura,

Attaching BrightEdge's latest redlines (BrightEdge_MSA_redlines_v2.docx) to the MSA and the draft order form. They pushed back hard on our standard feedback license and on the Order Form language that preserves customer output rights. High-level asks from procurement/legal below: 

- They want explicit assignment of derivative rights for outputs that incorporate their proprietary prompts/content (they keep arguing "ownership").
- A carveout that disallows Redwood from using customer prompts/content to train any model beyond debugging/ops (i.e., very restrictive training consent).
- A request for telemetry/telemetry retention evidence and an audit clause for model use.

We need a succinct internal position we can present back. My suggested starting points:
- Keep our position that customers own their input and output but we need a limited, nonexclusive feedback license for service improvement and safety unless they opt out via the Order Form.
- Offer a narrow training carveout: customer data won't be used to retrain foundation models; allow aggregated and anonymized signal for heuristic improvements or safety tuning with a 30-day opt-out after go-live.
- For law/ procurement: propose an evidence pack (logs + telemetry summary) and an on-site audit window limited to scope and frequency.

Actions: can you both review the attached redlines and mark the absolute non-negotiables (from legal / from sales/CS standpoint) by EOD today? I want to align before we reply to Amir.

Thanks — Steph

--

Thanks Steph — quick summary from my recent calls with Amir and Rachel:

- Customer concern: They want to ensure any model-derived feature (summaries, classifiers) can be productized by them if it’s derived primarily from their content. They equate that with "assignment\."
- Procurement is OK with a feedback/telemetry license for improving the hosted service, but not training on customer-provided prompts or labeled outputs.
- Timelines: procurement wants clean language to sign off this week so they can finalize procurement cycles.

My practical asks for legal:
1) If we offer an explicit "no retrain" commitment in the Order Form limited to BrightEdge-provided content, can we then request a limited, revocable research/feedback license that allows us to improve the service (not train foundation models) and that excludes product-derivative assignment?
2) On assignment: can we propose a narrowly scoped joint-ownership/usage license for features built on aggregated signals rather than a full assignment? That is, BrightEdge keeps output rights for their direct outputs, but Redwood retains rights to general improvements and aggregated feature engineering.

Notes: they called out telemetry retention and evidence for compliance. If we can provide a simple evidence pack and an audit window (Laura — scope please), it will go a long way.

Attaching my redline comments as inline notes in the doc.

—Ben

Thanks — I reviewed the BrightEdge redlines. High-level legal positions and proposed compromise language below (these are my suggested non-negotiables and concession windows):

Non-negotiables (we should not accept assignment):
- No assignment of Redwood's pre-existing models, IP, or improvements that are model-level (we can’t assign away our entire model outputs or core enhancements).
- No customer unilateral right to copy/build a competing service using Redwood's inference stack.

Concession windows (proposed draft language):
- Output rights: "Customer retains rights to outputs generated solely from Customer-provided inputs. Redwood and Customer agree that Redwood may use aggregated, anonymized signals derived from Customer usage to improve the Service, provided such signals cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct Customer proprietary content."
- Training consent: "Redwood will not use Customer-provided content to train or fine-tune foundation models used in the Service, except: (i) to the extent required for debugging and service quality improvements; and (ii) for aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry used for system-wide improvements. Customer may opt out of (ii) by updating the Order Form prior to go-live or by executing the attached Opt-Out Exhibit."
- Audit and evidence: offer a quarterly telemetry summary (token counts, retention periods, security controls) and a single annual on-site or remote compliance review with pre-defined scope and NDA specifics.

If we adopt that language, I think sales can present it as a good-faith compromise while protecting core IP. If BrightEdge insists on assignment, we should escalate to execs.

I marked precise clause edits in the attached doc (see comments). Please confirm and I'll prepare a clean counter to send to their counsel.

—Laura

Stephanie / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Mei (our counsel) and I discussed and we can move on a compromise if Redwood will accept these concrete items in the Order Form: 

1) Assignment-lite: BrightEdge keeps exclusive rights to outputs "to the extent such outputs are direct derivations of BrightEdge raw inputs and are unique to BrightEdge's datasets." 2) Training carveout: Redwood will not use BrightEdge inputs for retraining foundation or fine-tuned models used by other customers. Redwood may use samples for debugging only and with prior notice.
3) Evidence: bring a telemetry summary and agree to a single annual compliance review.

If you can incorporate language for 1) and 2) above and provide the telemetry summary template, we are prepared to move forward this week. I'll ask procurement to prepare the signature path upon receipt of your counter.
